fixes.explanation: A mystery would keep us guessing, but the verse is plain. The LORD says, "…I will make you an everlasting pride, a joy from age to age." (Isaiah 60:15) Zion has been forsaken and despised, and the LORD is the One who makes her an everlasting pride. The word that finishes it is joy.

Right, they don't stay away. Isaiah says, "Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn." (Isaiah 60:3) So the world is dark, and nations and even kings are coming to Zion's light. I'd show up for that too.

Yes, her own children. Isaiah says, "your sons will come from afar, and your daughters will be carried on the arm." (Isaiah 60:4) Sons coming from afar, daughters carried on the arm. Now that's a picture.

Deserts are a fair guess, friend, but this verse says something else. Isaiah says, "…the riches of the sea will be brought to you…" (Isaiah 60:5) The riches in this verse are the riches of the sea, along with the wealth of the nations.

It's true, actually. Isaiah says they come "…bearing gold and frankincense and proclaiming the praises of the LORD." (Isaiah 60:6) They show up with gold and frankincense in their hands and the LORD's praises on their lips. Gifts AND praise, friend. Hard to top that.

Yes, the ships of Tarshish. The LORD says, "Surely the islands will wait for Me, with the ships of Tarshish in the lead, to bring your children from afar…" (Isaiah 60:9) They're in the lead. Front of the line, friend.

Not empty-handed, friend. The LORD says the ships will bring Zion's children from afar "…with their silver and gold, to the honor of the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, for He has glorified you." (Isaiah 60:9) They arrive with silver and gold, and it's all for the honor of the LORD.
Wrath doesn't come after the favor here. The LORD says, "Although I struck you in anger, yet in favor I will show you mercy." (Isaiah 60:10) What He shows in favor is mercy.

False, you've got it. Isaiah says, "The sons of your oppressors will come and bow down to you; all who reviled you will fall facedown at your feet…" (Isaiah 60:14) The sons of her oppressors come to bow down. And those who reviled her fall facedown at her feet.
Yes, the LORD Himself. Isaiah says, "…the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your splendor." (Isaiah 60:19) The sun and moon are no longer her light, and the LORD is.
